definition: Flatten means to make something flat, so that whatever had height loses it.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word flatten. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know flatten should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: One hailstorm flattened the wheat that a whole dry summer had spared.
Smooth does much less than flatten — it only erases the surface's ridges while the shape underneath keeps its height; flattening presses the whole shape down toward level.
Crush goes further than flatten — a flattened box is still a neat, usable sheet; a crushed one is wreckage.

Level aims at evenness — a graded road, a floor, a playing field brought to one height. Flatten names a loss instead: whatever had height gives it up entirely. You can level a bumpy lawn and it is still a lawn; flatten a hedge and its shape is gone.

Squash is the informal, kitchen-floor word: flatness produced by sudden force, a grape under a heel. Flatten is calmer and more general — you can flatten a box slowly and neatly, on purpose, and what is flattened survives as a tidy sheet rather than a burst mess.

The print shop's oldest machine is a hand-cranked press, and its whole job is pressure.
Fresh paper arrives with a slight wave to it, so the printers flatten each stack first, leaving it under iron weights overnight until every sheet lies as thin and true as the tabletop.
Nothing about the step is violent.
The weights come down slowly, the paper survives in perfect condition, and by morning the stack has simply given up its height.
Visitors sometimes ask why the crew bothers, since the paper already looks fine at a glance.
The foreman's answer never changes: ink forgives many sins, but it will not forgive a sheet that still remembers its curl.
